title: cmHC: Balancing Stream Mixing in Hyper-Connections via Geometric Contraction

details.title: cmHC: Balancing Stream Mixing in Hyper-Connections via Geometric Contraction
details.abstract: Manifold-constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC) extends residual connections to multiple streams and stabilizes residual propagation by constraining stream-mixing residual matrices to the Birkhoff polytope, the set of doubly stochastic matrices. In this work, we investigate how to effectively mix residual streams within the Birkhoff polytope . We reveal a mixing trade-off : when under-mixed residual matrices stay close to the vertices of the Birkhoff polytope, hyper-connections will degenerate into a set of nearly independent streams; when over-mixe d residual matrices are concentrated around the uniform barycenter of the polytope, streams will become less distinguishable from each other. We theoretically validate our findings by bounding the cumulative residual mixing, stream difference and gradient difference of mixing coefficients across layers. Motivated by these findings, we propose Contraction for Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (cmHC), an exact doubly stochastic method which geometrically contracts the Birkhoff polytope toward its interior. This contraction mitigates under-mixing by forcing the residual matrices to explore deeper into the polytope, with a provable stream mixing bound and no new parameterization. Moreover, we apply a moderate contraction at the shallow layers to prevent over-mixing, enabling stable gradient propagation on extremely large-scale model pretraining. Extensive experiments across dense and mixture-of-experts models at various parameter scales demonstrate the effectiveness and scalability of cmHC. We also develop fused operators for cmHC on Ascend NPUs, reducing hyper-connection execution latency by up to 44.8%.

title: Non-penetrating World Models

details.title: Non-penetrating World Models
details.abstract: 🚧 World models can generate amazing worlds, but they still walk through walls! 👻 🎮 Today's video world models can generate impressive interactive environments, but they often fail to respect basic physical boundaries. For example, when you press W toward a wall, the model may simply walk straight through it! 💡 We introduce NoPeWorld , a lightweight framework that helps video world models stop at obstacles instead of walking through them . Interestingly, we find that world models already encode collision information in their hidden states. NoPeWorld leverages this information to prevent physical violations without retraining the entire world model. 📊 We also introduce NoPeBench , a benchmark for evaluating whether world models respect physical boundaries. 🚀 Check out our demos and open-source resources! 🌐 Project & Demos | 💻 Code | 🤗 Dataset | 📄 Paper

title: Reading the Unreadable: Text-Aware Image Super-Resolution Needs Reasoning

details.title: Reading the Unreadable: Text-Aware Image Super-Resolution Needs Reasoning
details.abstract: [TL;DR] Text-aware image super-resolution (TAISR) needs reasoning! Humans can often read badly degraded text by reasoning over context: a word repeated elsewhere in the image, neighboring numbers on a ruler, or a familiar logo. Super-resolution (SR) models rely on local visual evidence alone, so they struggle with exactly this kind of text. 🔍 ReasonText is a human-curated benchmark that separates reasoning-required text from locally recoverable text, paired with GTTCA , a recognition-based metric that measures text restoration without text-detection errors. Across 12 recent SR models, including TAISR models built for text, accuracy on reasoning-required text stays below 25%. 💡 RTC (Reasoning Transfer via Captioning) is a training-free plug-in. An MLLM reasons out the degraded text and writes it into the caption of a frozen text-conditioned SR model. RTC improves all six text-conditioned SR models we tested, especially on reasoning-required text (e.g., DiT4SR: 24.5% → 45.8%). Surprisingly, DiT4SR + RTC, a general real-world SR model, outperforms UniT + RTC, a TAISR model built on the same backbone with extra text-aware modules. This suggests that reasoning should be a core design axis for future TAISR. 🤗 Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Jasonleex1995/ReasonText 🌐 Project page: https://jasonleex1995.github.io/TAISR_needs_Reasoning/ 💻 Code: https://github.com/jasonleex1995/TAISR_needs_Reasoning 📍 Accepted to NeurIPS 2026. Poster in Sydney: Wed, Dec 9 · Hall 1-4 · #S3613. Happy to answer questions here!

title: AeroRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation

details.title: AeroRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation
details.abstract: Hi everyone, we're the authors! AeroRSI lets a drone navigation policy fix its own failures: before each failure, it flies on from every candidate action, learns the ones it actually completes, and repeats on the failures that remain, since each repair uncovers the next one. Three rounds take a 2B VLA policy on TravelUAV from 46.4% to 67.5% success and halve its collisions, 10.6 points above AeroDPO (the prior SOTA baseline), with no extra human labels or inference cost. 🌐 Project page (with demo video): https://starsholic.github.io/AeroRSI/ 💻 Code: https://github.com/starsholic/AeroRSI 🤗 Models: https://huggingface.co/DavidWu1116/AeroRSI Happy to answer any questions!

title: PURE: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Multi-Granularity Multimodal Identity Matching

details.title: PURE: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Multi-Granularity Multimodal Identity Matching
details.abstract: Hi HF community! 👋 I’m one of the authors of PURE. Same design, different color: should two product listings count as a match? The answer depends on whether we care about the underlying product design or the specific variant. We introduce PURE , a diagnostic benchmark built from real-world e-commerce matching pairs , with 1,457 multiple-choice questions verified by domain experts across 14 tasks. It examines four capabilities involved in multimodal identity matching: Perception, Understanding, Reasoning, and Evidence-grounded Judgment , with explicit distinctions between base-level and variant-level matching. A few interesting findings from our evaluation of 10 multimodal LLMs: Understanding scores highest on average, while evidence-grounded judgment scores lowest. Locating visual differences and applying variant-level matching rules remain challenging. Models can incorrectly report attribute conflicts between records that actually match. The pattern changes with granularity: most models recognize matching pairs more accurately than non-matching pairs at the base level, while the reverse holds at the variant level. We hope PURE helps the community identify weaknesses that aggregate matching accuracy can hide, and provides a useful testbed for improving multimodal grounding and matching. 📊 Dataset and evaluation code We’d love to hear your thoughts and see how your models perform!

title: AgentRoboCritic: Understanding the Capability of Frontier Agents on Direct Robot Control

details.title: AgentRoboCritic: Understanding the Capability of Frontier Agents on Direct Robot Control
details.abstract: 🤖 Can frontier agents control robots directly with low-level actions? And how do we actually tell how good they are? 📉 Existing evaluations focus on episode-level scores such as success rates. They hide the action-level feedback that is key to improving embodied agents! 💡 We introduce AgentRoboCritic . The policy agent states a local intent alongside each action, and a critic evaluates every action against it. For a failed action, the critic also returns its failure mode. With GPT-6 Astra as the critic, we annotate 12,844 actions across 12 manipulation benchmarks. 🔍 What the action-level feedback reveals: Closed-loop recovery: 49.8% of successful episodes contain at least one failed action, and 57.7% of failed actions are recovered by the end of the episode. Reliable semantic grounding: acting on the wrong object, order or category accounts for only 0.2% of failed actions. Strong zero-shot manipulation: GPT-6 Astra succeeds in 91% of RoboTwin 2.0 and 90% of YAMLab episodes, where π0.5 reaches 6% and 0%. The remaining bottleneck is physical execution: Grasp is the leading failure mode on most benchmarks. 🚀 To make action-level feedback low-cost, we release the 12,844 annotated actions, a 400-action human-annotated benchmark, and a fine-tuned Muse-Glimmer-30B critic. Its failure-mode accuracy rises from 32.6% to 74.2%, at over 30× lower cost than GPT-6 Astra. 🌐 Project page | 💻 Code | 🤗 Dataset | 📊 Benchmark | 🧠 Critic model | 📄 Paper

title: AutoPILOT: A Visual Agent Harness for Real-Time Gameplay

details.title: AutoPILOT: A Visual Agent Harness for Real-Time Gameplay
details.abstract: This paper identifies a largely overlooked bottleneck in real-time visual agents: conventional harnesses execute only one action per model call, forcing agents to act slowly on stale observations. AutoPILOT allows models to delegate execution to open-loop macros or model-written closed-loop visual controllers, and introduces AFK-Bench, a benchmark of 120 games that continue running during inference. Without changing the underlying model, AutoPILOT improves GPT-6.1 Sol’s real-time success rate from 38.3% to 68.6% over VISTA while reducing cost, showing that how model outputs are executed over time is a central dimension of agent design.

title: ViDecide: Teaching Video Diffusion Models to Reason and Plan Step by Step

details.title: ViDecide: Teaching Video Diffusion Models to Reason and Plan Step by Step
details.abstract: We release ViDecide: Teaching video diffusion models to reason and plan step by step , which explores whether video diffusion models can reason and plan step by step, like the way language models do. Current video models often break physical or logical rules in multi-step reasoning and planning, even when the final frame looks right. We trace this to the conventional training paradigm, which generates a solution as one fixed-length clip instead of a chain of decisions. ViDecide makes three changes: 🧩 Causal generation with adaptive termination : the model generates one state transition at a time and decides when to stop with a visual EOS frame. 🎯 Decision-focused training schedule : training focuses on high noise levels, where the next move is decided. 🔁 Corrective Fine-tuning (CFT) : a new post-training method for autoregressive video diffusion. It maps the noise of a failed decision to the model's own successful continuation, avoiding the inaccurate credit assignment and unstable policy gradients of diffusion RL. On rule-based games (VideoRLVR), multi-step planning tasks (VBVR), and our new robot benchmark RoboTwin-Plan, ViDecide reaches an average strict success rate of 83.8% , vs. 23.3% for standard fine-tuning and 67.8% for the strongest prior method, and generalizes to larger puzzles and unseen layouts. Code, models, and data are open-sourced: 📄 Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26389 🌐 Project page: https://kevin-thu.github.io/ViDecide 💻 Code: https://github.com/Kevin-thu/ViDecide A ⭐ or an upvote would mean a lot, and we'd love to hear your thoughts! 🙏

title: GameAnything: From Any Inspirations to Playable Game Worlds

details.title: GameAnything: From Any Inspirations to Playable Game Worlds
details.abstract: GameAnything: From Any Inspirations to Playable Game Worlds AI-driven game development holds the potential to transform diverse human inspirations into interactive experiences. However, existing systems and benchmarks primarily focus on explicit development specifications, with limited support for adapting multimodal references and evaluating actual gameplay experiences. We introduce GameAnything , an open-source agentic platform that transforms multimodal inspirations into playable extensions of existing games through iterative development. GameAnything integrates coding agents with an independent playtesting critic, persistent development state, and reusable experience memory to support continuous refinement. We further present GameAnything-Bench , a benchmark spanning diverse reference modalities, game creation objectives, and gaming environments, with exploratory gameplay testing to assess both functional correctness and gameplay quality. Evaluations of nine coding agent configurations reveal that current agents can adapt reference content but still struggle with playable interactions and precise modifications. Moreover, multimodal references improve content fidelity, while iterative refinement yields substantial but varying improvements across agents. These findings highlight both the potential and remaining challenges of inspiration-driven game development.

title: WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce

details.title: WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce
details.abstract: We present WeMM-Ecom, a family of multimodal large language models that deliver frontier e-commerce capabilities while achieving state-of-the-art general-purpose performance at their respective scales. The family spans five sizes, from a 0.8B dense model to a 35B mixture-of-experts model with 3B active parameters. Our training pipeline begins with two-stage continued pre-training that progressively raises the proportion of e-commerce data within a diverse multimodal data mixture, followed by hybrid-thinking post-training that combines on-policy distillation and reinforcement learning to support both non-thinking and thinking modes. For evaluation, we construct a comprehensive suite of 28 e-commerce benchmarks (23 in-house and five open-source) covering eight business scenarios and complement it with 64 public general-purpose benchmarks. On the e-commerce suite, WeMM-Ecom-35B-A3B surpasses substantially larger open-source flagship models, including Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, HY4, and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. On the general-purpose suite, every WeMM-Ecom model surpasses its similarly sized Qwen3.5 counterpart, with the lightweight variants (e.g., WeMM-Ecom-2B) showing clear advantages over leading lightweight models such as Qwen3.5-2B, MiniCPM-V-4.7-1B, and LFM3-VL-2B. Beyond benchmarks, WeMM-Ecom now powers hundreds of production use cases in WeChat, including catalog management, multimodal product search, and livestream commerce, serving billion-scale requests per day. We publicly release all model weights and detail our data curation, training recipe, and benchmark construction to facilitate future work on domain-specialized multimodal models.

title: HIVE-Bench: Evaluating Patch-Level Visual Representations for Egocentric Robot Manipulation

details.title: HIVE-Bench: Evaluating Patch-Level Visual Representations for Egocentric Robot Manipulation
details.abstract: Pretrained vision is a common start for robot learning, but most comparisons still score one pooled vector from a third-person image. Bimanual policies instead read dense patch tokens from cameras on the robot. We introduce HIVE-Bench: one shared flow-matching policy reads 20 encoders from seven families on 24 egocentric bimanual tasks, across adaptation, task sharing, and sweeps of data, model size, and layer. Keeping the patches matters. Averaging each view to one token removes most of the success, adaptation helps every pair we test, and one shared policy keeps most of the success of separate policies at a fraction of the updates. The same tokens are then scored with statistics, state and object readouts, published vision scores, and an inverse-dynamics readout. That readout of the commanded motion is one of the strongest measurements available before a policy is trained. Recognition, depth, and correspondence do not transfer reliably. Fine-tuning can improve the action readout even when other measurements move the other way, and no statistic is stable enough to replace a rollout before any deployment.

title: Distilling Visual Agents from Limited Interaction Experience

details.title: Distilling Visual Agents from Limited Interaction Experience
details.abstract: We study how much interaction experience is needed to distill capable visual agents. With just four selected trajectories per environment , offline OPD improves a Qwen3.5-4B student from 49.17% to 82.08% on Navigation and 60.16% to 85.55% on Sokoban , recovering over 90% of the measured gap to a 27B teacher on these panels. Training reuses recorded multimodal histories while generating fresh student responses and teacher feedback, requiring no new environment interaction during optimization . We also study few-task online OPD, matched SFT, and transfer to a 9B student across three visual environments. Code, examples, and results: https://github.com/elated-sawyer/visual-agent-distillation

details.title: UUBench: Understanding the Unspoken toward Full-Duplex Multimodal Interaction

We built UUBench to evaluate how well avatars pick up on those cues and respond appropriately. This is still a work in progress project, and we’d love your feedback! title: Embodied-Harness: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Robotic Manipulation

details.title: Embodied-Harness: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Robotic Manipulation
details.abstract: Can a robot improve across attempts while its model parameters stay frozen? In Embodied-Harness , we explore recursive self-improvement (RSI) for robotic manipulation. The Actor follows operational guidance to carry out a task. After a failed attempt, the Reflector uses the execution trace and prior experience to diagnose what went wrong and revise that guidance. The Actor then tries again with the revised guidance, and the new execution trace informs the next round of reflection. Embodied-Harness achieves success rates of 82.4% on RoboTwin 2.0 , 76.7% on RoboSPA , and 94.4% on RMBench . On three real-world manipulation tasks, it achieves an average success rate of 96.7% .

title: A Pipeline-Parallel System for Depth-Recurrent Models

details.title: A Pipeline-Parallel System for Depth-Recurrent Models
details.abstract: Depth-recurrent (Looped) models raise effective depth by applying a shared stack of blocks several times. Scaling them usually requires pipeline parallelism, but commonly used interleaved 1F1B is drawn for an acyclic stage graph in which each micro-batch enters each stage once. Once that stack is split across stages, the same stage is visited several times on one micro-batch and later stages feed earlier ones: native 1F1B has no slot for the extra visit, cannot rank a first iteration against a second, and its neighbour-only send/receive order has no back edge to the first stage, so the arrangement stalls or fires out of order. We present Loop-PP, which rebuilds both the timetable and the communication for this cyclic layout. It schedules different iterations of the same stage separately, specializes a 1F1B skeleton into a globally consistent order over those visits, and emits a static instruction stream per rank that separates posting from waiting so communication overlaps local compute. Loop-PP is bit-identical to a single-stage reference. On 8B-60B MoE models, it lowers peak memory by as much as 32.8%, and with compute budget fixed, the best observed throughput rises by 12.7%.

title: SAVIOR: Sample-efficient Adaptation of Vision-Language Models for OCR Representation

details.title: SAVIOR: Sample-efficient Adaptation of Vision-Language Models for OCR Representation
details.abstract: Author here (Hyperbots). OCR and vision-language models do well on standard benchmarks but break on patterns common in finance documents: rotated and vertical text, vendor names inside logos, fine print, degraded scans and dense multi-column pages. SAVIOR-Train targets those cases with just 2,234 curated documents; fine-tuning Qwen2.5-VL-Instruct on it reaches 0.93 word recall. title: NoHairCache: Calibrate-Once KV Cache Eviction with One Power-Law Exponent

details.title: NoHairCache: Calibrate-Once KV Cache Eviction with One Power-Law Exponent
details.abstract: The decay exponent α in KV-cache eviction is an intrinsic property of the model: calibrated once on a single corpus, it transfers directly across domains. Attention-based accumulation (H2O) and recency-based sliding windows (StreamingLLM) are two dominant eviction frameworks, often treated as unrelated, but we show that they are the two endpoints of a single power-law family: by scoring each token as si=Ai⋅(t−i)−α, where Ai is cumulative attention and α controls the age penalty, H2O and StreamingLLM correspond to α=0 and α→∞, respectively (with StreamingLLM additionally hard-coding an attention-sink patch). The no-hair mechanism of \citet{xiang2026nohair} bounds the admissible range of α, and the measured exponents agree: calibrating once on WikiText yields [0.556,0.822] for a representative model (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct). The per-model ranges are consistent across five models (410M--1.5B) and independently match the optimal regions from perplexity sweeps. \textsc{NoHairCache} achieves the lowest perplexity across three datasets (WikiText, PG19, and arXiv) without per-dataset tuning, outperforming both H2O and StreamingLLM (p<0.05 on all three datasets, with 0.06--0.10 PPL gains over StreamingLLM at budget 512). On downstream four-way multiple-choice QA, it matches or outperforms StreamingLLM across all nine (task, budget) cells, retaining 98.2% of full-cache accuracy on NarrativeQA at 25% retention versus 91.1% for StreamingLLM; per-cell McNemar tests are not significant, so QA is corroborating only. We release our calibration script and drop-in scorer upon publication.

details.title: Fast-JEPA: Advancing the Success-Latency Frontier for Latent World Models

Fast-JEPA combines goal-directed action proposals with direct predictions of complete candidate outcomes, avoiding recursive state rollout during search refinement. 🚀 Across PushT, Reacher, Cube, and TwoRoom, it achieves 96.50% average success with 2.41× faster planning than our locally evaluated INTACT configuration. 🌍 We also introduce DynaGoal to evaluate planning under changing goals and environment geometry, execution deadlines, and controlled response delays. 💻 Training and evaluation code are now open source. title: Beyond Attention Maps: Understanding and Improving Medical MLLMs via Visual Values

details.title: Beyond Attention Maps: Understanding and Improving Medical MLLMs via Visual Values
details.abstract: Are We Overlooking the V in MLLMs Attention? Most existing studies on MLLMs focus on improving spatial attention — teaching models where to look. But does looking at the right region necessarily lead to a correct answer? In our recent work, Beyond Attention Maps: Understanding and Improving Medical MLLMs via Visual Values, we revisit this question using paired non-contrast and contrast-enhanced medical images. Our findings reveal that: 🔹 Highly similar attention maps can lead to drastically different predictions. 🔹 Intervening on visual values (V) produces substantially larger prediction changes than intervening on attention weights. 🔹 Informative visual values remain beneficial even when attention maps are heavily perturbed. Motivated by these observations, we propose VIVID, a visual value-guided on-policy distillation framework that uses the student's response to enhanced visual evidence to refine teacher supervision. Beyond medical imaging, we hope to inspire a broader discussion: Should we shift some of our attention from learning where to look towards learning what to retrieve? And for on-policy distillation, should we focus not only on what the teacher predicts, but also on how visual evidence shapes its supervision? 📄 Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29361 🌐 Project: https://qiuzyc.github.io/VIVID We welcome discussions and feedback from the community! #MLLM #VisualUnderstanding #Attention #OnPolicyDistillation #MedicalAI

title: MMMem: Self-Improving Agents with Task-Aware Multimodal Experience Consolidation

details.title: MMMem: Self-Improving Agents with Task-Aware Multimodal Experience Consolidation
details.abstract: We’re sharing MMMem, a multimodal memory framework that helps agents learn from completed tasks. MMMem turns past answers into reusable experiences, links them back to the original evidence, and retrieves them when they can help with a new question. Across three benchmarks and two vision-language models, MMMem outperformed the baselines we evaluated. We’d love to hear your feedback!

title: Deterministic, Reproducible Inference in Exact Integer Arithmetic, and Verifiable Distributed Inference as Its Consequence

details.title: Deterministic, Reproducible Inference in Exact Integer Arithmetic, and Verifiable Distributed Inference as Its Consequence
details.abstract: We present tritify, an open-source runtime that runs the forward pass of real models — decoder-only LLMs, MoE decoders, and the SAM 2.1 image/video stack — entirely in exact integer arithmetic, with floating point confined to offline quantization. The output is bit-identical across hardware and across CPU/GPU, reproduces the float reference's decisions with the numeric exceptions measured, and stays byte-identical when the model is split across machines. That last point is the payoff: verifiable distributed inference — an untrusted server or a fleet of devices runs the model while an open scalar oracle re-derives the exact bytes. Code: github.com/pelloran-inc/tritify

title: How Complete Must an Environment Be to Train a Capable GUI Agent?

details.title: How Complete Must an Environment Be to Train a Capable GUI Agent?
details.abstract: Graphical user interface (GUI) agents are widely trained in executable GUI environments. To lower cost, build environments in batches, and reduce manual effort, each work trades away part of the environment through its construction choices. We describe these choices along three dimensions: reward coverage, the goal-reaching trajectories the verifier rewards; data coverage, the application data the agent is exposed to beyond what the task reads or writes; and feature coverage, the application features beyond what the task uses. Existing works set each dimension on engineering grounds, but they do not measure its effect on training. How complete must an environment be to train a capable agent, and along which dimensions? In MobileGym, we adjust each dimension separately, train Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct, and evaluate every policy in the original full environment. A verifier that rewards only one reference path lowers success by 10.53 points, and removing unneeded records also lowers success. Pruning unneeded features instead raises success from 51.61% to 56.13%, entirely on tasks whose environments it left unchanged. The gain reverses when each episode is weighted equally and vanishes when only episodes on the pruned tasks are balanced. Without pruning, length weighting there reinforces long detour successes that erode skills on other tasks. Following these findings, we build MobileGym-Lite, which keeps reward and data coverage complete and prunes unneeded features. It outperforms Full in the full environment (55.48% versus 51.61% success) with lower construction cost.

title: SWEEP-Bench: Do Embodied Policies Act on the Speed They See?

details.title: SWEEP-Bench: Do Embodied Policies Act on the Speed They See?
details.abstract: We introduced SWEEP-Bench, a benchmark of 80 conveyor tasks at 13 belt speeds. Many fine-tuned policies tend to produce actions suited to the average demonstration speed, and our results suggest that past frames widen the speed range only for those pretrained on multiple frames. An estimated speed recovers most of the gain that policies obtain from the ground-truth speed.
